The 404 error handler uses request.url directly in a template string passed to render_template_string() without escaping. An attacker can inject malicious JavaScript via a crafted URL to execute XSS.
Exception message str(e) is concatenated directly into an HTML template passed to render_template_string(). Error messages containing user input can lead to reflected XSS attacks.
yaml.load() is called without specifying a safe Loader parameter. This allows arbitrary Python object deserialization and can lead to remote code execution when processing untrusted YAML files.
The insecure_verify() function decodes JWT tokens with verify=False, completely bypassing signature verification. This allows attackers to forge tokens and bypass authentication.
